Michelle Bowman.title: Fed Vice Chair of Supervision
Michelle Bowman.quote: “The more persistent higher oil prices are—or if we start to see broader effects of higher energy prices on PCE inflation—the more likely I will consider shifting my approach to thinking about the balance of risks.”

Jerome Powell.title: Governor
Jerome Powell.quote: “We’re right kind of at the high end of neutral or perhaps mildly restrictive. The labor market shows more and more signs of stability, whereas inflation is kind of misbehaving. And so maybe a little bit of restriction or the high end of neutral is just the right place to be.”

John Williams.title: New York Fed President
John Williams.quote: “My forecast personally is for inflation to come down in ⁠the second half of this year and come down further next year...if ​the economy is not on a trajectory that will bring inflation back down to 2% ... it would absolutely be appropriate to act.”

Philip Jefferson.title: Vice Chair
Philip Jefferson.quote: “This policy stance should continue to support the labor market while allowing inflation to resume its decline toward our 2% target.…In a scenario where actual ​inflation does not start to cool down soon, I believe that it could ⁠be appropriate to reconsider our current policy stance to ensure we fulfill our commitment to deliver price ​stability.”

Michael Barr.title: Governor
Michael Barr.quote: “I am particularly concerned that yet another price shock could increase longer-term inflation expectations.”

Chris Waller.title: Governor
Chris Waller.quote: “I will need to see several months of lower readings to feel that inflation is moving in the right direction.”

Anna Paulson.title: Philadelphia Fed President
Anna Paulson.quote: “If policy is appropriately calibrated, I would expect to see growing signs that inflation is coming down…. If instead underlying inflation remains stubbornly elevated, the passage of time without progress would itself signal that more restrictive policy is needed.”

Mary Daly.title: San Francisco Fed President
Mary Daly.quote: “I also hear a lot about, should we be making preemptive cuts, or hikes rather, and I don't see a lot of evidence that that's an urgent problem to solve….Policy is in a good place.”

Kevin Warsh.title: Chairman
Kevin Warsh.quote: “The path to central bank heaven requires delivering on our remit. These days that means delivering on price stability. I wouldn't measure that path in 42 days, or any one particular meeting.”

Lisa Cook.title: Governor
Lisa Cook.quote: “I would support an ​increase, if it becomes necessary, to bring inflation down. It may not.”

Thomas Barkin.title: Richmond Fed President
Thomas Barkin.quote: The July jobs report was "very consistent with how I've been seeing the labor market, which is: it's not loose, it's not tight.”

Alberto Musalem.title: St. Louis Fed President
Alberto Musalem.quote: “More gradual interest rate increases are preferable, better, less disruptive than later, potentially larger, potentially more abrupt increases.”

Neel Kashkari.title: Minneapolis Fed President
Neel Kashkari.quote: “My goal is not to slow the economy down….The goal is to ⁠get inflation ​back down to our 2% target.”

Lorie Logan.title: Dallas Fed President
Lorie Logan.quote: “Without any policy restraint, inflation will likely continue to trend above target until there's an unanticipated shock.”

Beth Hammack.title: Cleveland Fed President
Beth Hammack.quote: “One 25-basis-point move probably doesn't do a whole lot for the economy, so it's probably some number of movements, but I don't want to prejudge what that number is going to be.”

Austan Goolsbee.title: Chicago Fed President
Austan Goolsbee.quote: "I'm heartened by this CPI today but we need a lot more than one month to think that it is going well.”

Susan Collins.title: Boston Fed President
Susan Collins.quote: “While it is not in my most likely outlook, I could envision a scenario in which some policy tightening is needed to ensure that inflation returns durably to 2% in a timely manner.”

Jeffrey Schmid.title: Kansas City Fed President
Jeffrey Schmid.quote: “I believe that bringing inflation down to the Fed’s 2% objective will require tighter policy.”
